From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: SKU retrieval schema & SDK auth (Streamline)

Hi Lena — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can keep momentum: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: integrate Redwood to provide semantic SKU lookup + structured responses for downstream systems (inventory, pricing, recommendations).
- Primary flows: 1) interactive chat for agent-assist (tool-calling to return SKU JSON), 2) batch/async embedding-based reranking for search queries.

Open technical questions we flagged on the call (please confirm):
1) SDKs/langs: you said engineering uses Python and Node primarily — confirm if we should prepare sample snippets for both.
2) Auth model: do you prefer API keys scoped to environments, or short-lived service-account JWTs (OIDC) with tenant-scoped claims?
3) Routing: will requests include tenant_id + region header? Any existing proxy we should integrate with?
4) Structured output: do you want Redwood to use tool-calling (JSON schema) that returns a SKU object (sku_id, title, price, availability, match_score, debug_tokens)? Or prefer a completions-style JSON-in-text?
5) Embeddings / reranker: confirm index size (approx # SKUs) and expected QPS for embedding lookup. Also whether you need 1:1 re-rank scoring or full neural re-ranker.
6) Request/response semantics: confirm preferred mode for the agent flow — chat with tool-calls or completions with stop sequences? Any constraints on max_tokens for the structured payload?
7) Streaming: do you want partial streaming for agent responses while the reranker runs, and do streamed chunks include tool-call triggers?

Attachments & links
- Attached: a short integration proposal (PDF) and the call recording.
- Shared Drive: I put a sample carrier schema in the Drive link (see related links).

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
- You confirm 1–6 above by EOD Monday (7/27).
- We’ll produce: a) sample Python & Node SDK snippets for auth and routing, b) a suggested tool-calling JSON schema for SKU responses, and c) an embedding + rerank sizing doc by Wed (7/29).
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra & search lead — propose Tue 7/28 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 7/29 11:00–11:45 PT. Which works?

Questions for you to answer in reply: SDK langs (confirm), preferred auth (api-key / service account), approx SKU count and QPS, and whether you want streaming tool-calls.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben and Connor for the technical follow-up.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Next steps: SKU retrieval schema & SDK auth (Streamline)

Vanessa — thanks for the summary, that matches our view. Quick answers inline: 

1) SDKs/langs: yes please provide Python + Node samples. Our backend services are in Python (FastAPI) and we have a Node-based edge service for routing.

2) Auth model: prefer short-lived service accounts (JWT) issued by our credential broker. We want RBAC for dev/stage/prod and scoping by tenant_id.

3) Routing: will include tenant_id header and a region code (us/eu). We do have an Envoy sidecar at the edge today; we can add headers there.

4) Structured output: strongly prefer a deterministic JSON tool-calling approach — consumers will deserialize directly into our downstream pipelines. Please propose a strict JSON schema.

5) Embeddings / reranker: ~350k SKUs, mixed catalog (US + EU). Peak QPS for search ~120 qps, average 35 qps. We want vector-store + light neural re-ranker on top (not full cross-attention re-rank).

6) Request/response semantics: prefer chat + tool-calling for the agent flow (keeps context and allows function-call-like responses). For batch scoring/completions (eg. autosuggest) we may use completions with stop tokens for concise payloads. Regarding max_tokens: our downstream prefers bounded payloads — ideally < 1024 tokens for structured outputs.

7) Streaming: good to support streaming of human-facing messages, but tool-call payloads should be delivered atomically. If streaming is implemented, it should buffer tool-call JSON until complete.

I attached a small sanitized SKU sample CSV (streamline-sku-sample.csv) to this reply.

Let’s take Tue 7/28 10:00 PT for the deep-dive (that works for our infra lead). Please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Lena
Director, Search & Catalog
Streamline AI
Lena.Park@streamline.ai

Subject: Re: Next steps: SKU retrieval schema & SDK auth (Streamline)

Thanks Lena — good data and thanks Vanessa for the recap. A few technical clarifications and a minimal proposal so we’re ready for Tue’s deep-dive: 

Quick tech proposals (minimal viable integration)
- SDK snippets: we’ll provide a Python FastAPI example showing service-account JWT exchange (short-lived token) and a Node edge example that sets tenant_id / region headers.
- Auth: support OIDC/JWT service accounts + API keys for quick POC. Tokens should include tenant_id claim for routing.
- Routing: header-based routing (X-Redwood-Tenant, X-Redwood-Region) that our smart routing layer can use to pick a model pool (hosted/dedicated) and apply SLAs.

Suggested tool-calling JSON schema (minimal fields)
- sku_search_response: {
  "sku_id": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "price_cents": "integer",
  "availability": "IN_STOCK|OUT_OF_STOCK|BACKORDER",
  "match_score": "float",
  "source": "string",
  "debug_tokens": "optional string or tokenized snippet for QA"
}

Notes on chat vs completions / tokenization
- Chat + tool-calling: recommended for agent flows where state and follow-up calls matter. We treat the schema as the tool response — the runtime will return a single JSON object when the tool is invoked.
- Completions: acceptable for short batch payloads (autosuggest), but you’ll need stop sequences (e.g., "\n\n") and strict post-parse validation.
- max_tokens guidance: for structured SKU JSON we recommend capping model output to 1024 tokens to be safe; for average SKU object expect ~150–300 tokens depending on description length.
- Streaming semantics: streaming human messages is supported. Tool-call responses (JSON schema) should be sent as a single atomic message once fully generated; partial JSON fragments in stream are error-prone for downstream deserializers.

Embeddings / rerank notes
- For ~350k vectors we recommend an ANN index (HNSW) + a small re-ranker that takes the top-K (e.g., 25) and scores with a cheap cross-encoder (if you want higher precision).
- Vector dims: we support multiple dims (768/1536/2048). If you want to reuse off-the-shelf models we can recommend 1536 for good accuracy/latency tradeoff.

Deliverables before Tue 7/28
- Python + Node SDK snippets and auth samples (by EOD Mon 7/27)
- Proposed JSON schema for sku_search_response (attached as a one-page doc inside the PDF)
- A short embedding sizing estimate (vectors, memory, expected latency)

I’ll attach the call recording and point to the internal architecture note for the deep-dive. Vanessa — can you send the calendar invite for Tue 7/28 10:00 PT and include our infra lead Connor + your technical PM?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
